# 2026 Service Plan process
The Service Plan is Sound Transit’s annual planning process for
managing our regional transit network that informs our operating
budget  The Service Plan evaluates and proposes changes to
coordinate with the opening of high-capacity transit projects, improve
performance, respond to ridership trends, and optimize our operating
resources  The Service Plan is also the vehicle for the Sound Transit
Board of Directors (Board) to approve any “major service changes,”
as defined by Sound Transit-adopted policy
This year’s plan looks a bit different, as we are delivering
the Service Plan in two parts:
• Part one, the  Rail Service Plan , proposes minor service
changes for Link light rail and Sounder commuter rail  The Board
reviewed this portion in October 2025; Board action is not
required for these minor rail changes
• Part two, the  Bus Service Plan , will propose minor and major
ST Express bus service changes  We hosted public engagement
on these changes in fall 2025  Board consideration will occur
in early 2026  Board action is required for the major service
changes proposed in the plan  The bus changes will come in fall
2026 at the earliest, after the 2026 Men’s FIFA World Cup
We will implement the plans during our regionally coordinated service
changes in spring (March) and fall (August) of 2026

# Overview of recent ridership trends
The Lynnwood Link Extension leads to
increased ridership on the 1 Line
The Lynnwood Link Extension extended the 1 Line from Northgate to
Lynnwood City Center on August 30, 2024  Ridership on the 1 Line
has increased substantially since the completion of the Lynnwood
Link Extension project  May 2025 had the highest monthly ridership
for any month in Link history, with 3,091,000 boardings, an average
of 105,600 daily boardings  Since the 1 Line began serving the new
stations north of Northgate, monthly ridership has experienced an
average year-over-year growth of 25%
> Figure 1: 1 Line Monthly Ridership, January 2023 - July 2025
2 Line ridership grows after service
extension to Downtown Redmond
Monthly ridership on the 2 Line has fluctuated since service began
in April 2024  Initial months saw rapid growth, with ridership peaking
at over 186,000 boardings in May 2024 before declining in winter,
reaching a low of about 69,600 boardings in February 2025  This
variability in ridership is most likely due to seasonal changes in
ridership demand, with most services having decreased ridership
during the winter months  A significant increase in ridership occurred
in May 2025 when service extended to Downtown Redmond  That
month, ridership increased to over 214,000 boardings, followed by
similarly high figures in June and a record high of more than 306,000
boardings in July 2025, indicating that the extension had a substantial
effect on demand

# What is a major service
Sound Transit Board of Directors’ policy defines a major service
change as any single change in service on an individual bus or rail
route that would:
• Add or eliminate more than 25% of the route’s weekly revenue
service hours, and/or;
• Permanently move the location of a bus stop by more than a
quarter mile, or rail station by more than a half-mile, and/or;
• Close or eliminate a bus stop or rail station without a
replacement of any kind within a quarter mile of bus stops or a
half-mile of rail stations

The first phase, which included a survey that asked the public about
service priorities, was completed in April 2025
Key takeaways from the survey included:
• Respondents reported that they used Route 545, 550, and 594
• The most popular trip purpose was to commute to/from work,
followed closely by recreational trips
• About half said they would be able to use the 1 Line or 2 Line for
all or most of their trips after the Link extensions open
• Several riders expressed concerns about changes to bus service
that could increase travel time or add transfers to trips
The second phase of engagement, which informed the public about
rail changes coming in 2026, was conducted between July 28 and
August 11, 2025  Sound Transit shared upcoming rail changes
through a variety of engagement methods, including:
Website updates
Social media posts
Tabling at fairs and festivals
For the new Pinehurst Station, construction engagement has been
conducted since 2023  In fall 2024, a survey collected public input
on a station name  The station name was adopted in January 2025
Staff informed the public about the Pinehurst service change through
phase two engagement
In September 2025, we also asked riders about shifting the
southbound Sounder N Line schedule to earlier (removing 7:45 a  m
trip and replacing it with 5:45 a  m trip)  The Sounder N Line survey
received 780+ responses  About 70% of respondents said they
preferred the current southbound schedule  Currently, a change to
the southbound Sounder N Line schedule is not recommended
The third phase of engagement focused on collecting feedback on
the proposed 2026 ST Express bus service changes  This phase of
engagement occurred between October 6 and November 11, 2025

2026 ST Express bus service proposals
